title: QNu Labs Launches QShield 2.0 to Drive India’s National Cryptographic Assessment & Assurance Framework - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Bengaluru-based QNu Labs launched QShield 2.0, a sovereign post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility platform built to serve as the execution engine for India's National Cryptographic Assessment & Assurance Framework, timed to a government mandate that critical infrastructure begin formal PQC migration by 2027.

insights.claim: QNu Labs, a Bengaluru-based quantum security startup, launched QShield 2.0 — a sovereign, full-stack post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and crypto-agility platform — at the company's 10th anniversary event, positioning it as the core execution engine for India's National Cryptographic Assessment & Assurance Framework (NCAAF).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Being named the core engine of a named national framework signals QNu Labs is positioning itself as the default vendor for India's sovereign PQC compliance market, not just one option among many.

insights.claim: The QShield 2.0 release aligns with recommendations from the Department of Science and Technology's National Quantum Mission (NQM) Task Force Report, which mandates that critical infrastructure sectors initiate formal PQC migration by 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hard 2027 regulatory deadline for critical infrastructure (banks, defense, national security depositories) creates a concrete, time-boxed compliance-driven demand curve for PQC vendors serving the Indian market — a catalyst to track for accelerating enterprise procurement over the next 12-18 months.

insights.claim: The NCAAF architecture is structured as an iterative three-stage workflow: Discover (mapping cryptographic assets across legacy IT/OT networks), Assess (scoring algorithms and certificates against quantum vulnerability windows), and Assure (continuous, real-time posture validation).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This Discover-Assess-Assure cycle is a reusable compliance framework that other national or enterprise PQC-readiness programs could adopt, and QNu Labs' early alignment with it gives it a template advantage over competitors building generic PQC tools.

insights.claim: QShield 2.0 consolidates five operational modules into a unified management plane: Quantum Entropy (hardware QRNG via Tropos backends), Quantum Readiness Risk Assessment (automated discovery/classification/scoring), Quantum PKI (crypto-agile certificate authority and identity lifecycle), Quantum Vault (hardware-secured key custody), and AI Security (cryptographic verification for AI models and pipelines).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A single consolidated platform spanning entropy generation, PKI, key custody, and AI security lowers integration friction for sovereign buyers (banks, defense agencies) versus stitching together point solutions, which is a competitive moat if adoption sticks.

insights.claim: QShield 2.0 is built for on-premises sovereign deployment in banks, defense agencies, and critical infrastructure, explicitly designed to address 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' attack vectors and AI-driven attack surfaces.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Targeting 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' explicitly frames the product around the near-term risk that adversaries are already stockpiling encrypted data to decrypt once cryptographically-relevant quantum computers arrive, reinforcing urgency of PQC migration regardless of when quantum computers actually mature.
insights.quote: address “Harvest Now, Decrypt Later” attack vectors and AI-driven attack surfaces

insights.claim: The AI Security module extends QShield 2.0's scope beyond classic PQC into AI supply-chain integrity, covering signed model weights, prompt/data pipeline integrity, and agentic AI identity verification.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is a non-obvious convergence of quantum-safe cryptography and AI governance/security — QNu Labs is betting that cryptographic verification (signed weights, pipeline integrity, agentic identity) becomes a required layer of AI infrastructure, which broadens its addressable market beyond pure PQC compliance into AI security tooling.

insights.claim: QNu Labs was incubated at IIT Madras Research Park and is supported by India's National Quantum Mission; its existing hardware-software portfolio includes Armos Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Tropos QRNG systems, both listed on India's Government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement portal.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GeM listing gives QNu Labs a pre-existing direct sales channel into Indian government agencies without a separate tender process, which should shorten the sales cycle for QShield 2.0 relative to a vendor without that access.

insights.claim: The QShield 2.0 launch incorporates initial deployment accounts across major Indian commercial banks and national security depositories.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early named-sector traction (banks, national security depositories) at launch, even without disclosed counts or revenue, suggests the product is already past pure pilot stage in at least some regulated verticals — worth tracking for named customers or contract values in follow-up coverage.
